title: The Railroad Hour
paragraphs: Weekly musical-drama anthology sponsored by the Association of American Railroads, starring Gordon MacRae in condensed operettas, Broadway musicals and original musical stories. Frozen GRH snapshot has 244 dated broadcasts plus two undated reference tracks.

GRH documents the program through ABC 45-minute era (October 4, 1948 to April 18, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], ABC 30-minute era (April 25, 1949 to September 26, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and NBC 30-minute era (October 3, 1949 to June 21, 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Gordon MacRae (host on 221 recordings, performer on 221 recordings, composer on 1 recording, director on 1 recording, and narrator on 1 recording), Marvin Miller (announcer on 215 recordings, performer on 52 recordings, and narrator on 1 recording), Norman Luboff (performer on 210 recordings, choir director on 208 recordings, conductor on 9 recordings, composer on 1 recording, and director on 1 recording), Carmen Dragon (conductor on 215 recordings, preparer on 51 recordings, composer on 9 recordings, arranger on 8 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Robert E. Lee (radio adaptor on 98 recordings, writer on 26 recordings, composer on 25 recordings, producer on 8 recordings, performer on 3 recordings, and author on 1 recording), Jerome Lawrence (radio adaptor on 98 recordings, writer on 26 recordings, composer on 25 recordings, producer on 7 recordings, performer on 3 recordings, and author on 1 recording), and Dorothy Warenskjold (performer on 57 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include music, theater and performance, royalty, aristocracy and court society, travel and journeys, romance, courtship and marriage, war and military settings, and American historical and regional settings.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar railroad-industry public relations, Broadway and operetta repertoire on network radio, and Late network-radio prestige programming.
